title: Exploring Photographs, Lesson 3: Methods of Visual Analysis
evidence_scope: Separates description, reflection, and formal analysis and supplies looking questions.
limitations: A teaching lesson, not a validated universal scoring model.

title: 2026 Contest judging process
evidence_scope: States current contest stages, criteria, and progressive introduction of context.
limitations: Applies primarily to photojournalism and documentary competition judging.

title: 2026 Contest code of ethics
evidence_scope: Defines ethical expectations for documentary and photojournalistic entries.
limitations: A contextual gate for relevant uses, not an aesthetic score for every photograph.

title: 2026 Contest verification process
evidence_scope: Documents manipulation review, original-file checks, fact checking, and disclosure requirements.
limitations: Contest-specific rules; do not impose them on disclosed conceptual or commercial work.

title: Aperture On Sight: Teaching Visual Literacy through Photography
evidence_scope: A full curriculum connecting close looking, image reading, storytelling, and photobook making.
limitations: Educational prompts require adaptation before use as critique rules.

title: Joel Meyerowitz: Seeing Things
evidence_scope: Official description confirms thirty photographs with short commentaries on light, gesture, composition, story, layers, and fleeting moments.
limitations: The full commentaries are not available on the product page; do not infer their content.

title: The Photographer's Eye
author_org: Museum of Modern Art / John Szarkowski
evidence_scope: Official MoMA publication announcement documents the book's critical perspective on photographic seeing.
limitations: This record is the announcement rather than a complete digitized book; verify chapter-level claims elsewhere.

title: Wear Good Shoes: Advice from Magnum Photographers
evidence_scope: First-party collection of short advice from Magnum photographers.
limitations: Short quotations are prompts, not evidence for universal visual rules.

title: Susan Meiselas on Building Relationships With Subjects
evidence_scope: First-party practice discussion centered on relationships with photographed people.
limitations: Practice insight from one photographer; do not turn it into a mandatory street-photography style.

title: Creative Documentary and Photojournalism Program
evidence_scope: Official program description documents assignments, feedback, critique, editing, sequencing, and exhibition work.
limitations: A high-cost professional program description, not proof of learning outcomes or a beginner recommendation.

title: Alec Soth: Cleansing the Visual Palate
evidence_scope: First-party interview material on responding to rooms, windows, light, surfaces, and people without forcing a grand narrative.
limitations: Article contains multiple works; cite an exact named image and position when used as a reference.

title: Education at Aperture
evidence_scope: Official hub for Aperture's visual literacy and photography education resources.
limitations: A hub, not a direct source for a specific critique claim.

title: 艾伦沙勒讲解：8张照片构图技巧
author_org: 光尘记 / original creator Alan Schaller
evidence_scope: Chinese translation/voiceover of an Alan Schaller lesson using eight photographs.
limitations: Uploader states the video belongs to the original creator; trace claims and images to Alan Schaller before promotion into a rule card.

title: 学习构图的底层方法论（从零学摄影07期）
evidence_scope: A popular Chinese-language course episode explicitly challenging recipe-only composition learning.
limitations: Popularity is discovery evidence only; claims, examples, and exercises still require source-by-source review.

title: Tatiana Hopper: Photography & Filmmaking
evidence_scope: Creator's official index of educational photography videos.
limitations: Use individual videos only after checking sources, exact works, and whether analysis supports the diagnosed problem.

title: The Photographic Eye / TPE Tribe
evidence_scope: Official description of a feedback-centered photography education community and the educator's background.
limitations: Self-description and testimonials do not establish critique accuracy or independent learning outcomes.

title: Reading Visual Images
evidence_scope: Eight-hour introductory course on analyzing photographs as social data, including context, documentary evidence, truth, uncertainty, and cultural diversity.
limitations: Social-science interpretation course rather than a camera-craft or image-editing curriculum.

title: Community Photo Stories
evidence_scope: Official lesson asks students to photograph their communities from varied viewpoints and connect compositional choices with narrative perspective.
limitations: Designed for grades 6–12; adapt prompts rather than assuming adult or advanced critique depth.

title: Focus on Photography: A Curriculum Guide
evidence_scope: ICP curriculum guide links photographic history, technique, aesthetics, practice, visual literacy, and how images communicate meaning.
limitations: School-oriented curriculum; individual exercises require page-level review before direct reuse.

title: The Evolution of the Book: Introducing Students to Visual Analysis
evidence_scope: Official primary-source lesson includes close description and discussion of perspective in an Ansel Adams photograph.
limitations: Broader visual-literacy lesson rather than a comprehensive photography curriculum.

title: Larry Fink on Composition and Improvisation: Learning Guide
evidence_scope: Official guide organizes Fink's first-person teaching into discussion topics, named images, vocabulary, and assignments about layered social scenes, rhythm, conflict, harmony, and chance.
limitations: Guide excerpts and interprets a paid book; inspect the cited image and page before attributing a specific claim.

title: Todd Hido on Landscapes, Interiors, and the Nude: Learning Guide
evidence_scope: Official guide structures Hido's practice around landscape, interiors, available light, subtle narrative detail, accident, and coincidence.
limitations: A single photographer's atmospheric practice; do not universalize deliberate ambiguity or night treatment.

title: This Equals That: Learning Guide
evidence_scope: Official learning guide uses paired photographs and vocabulary to teach association, framing, abstraction, focus, space, balance, and sequencing.
limitations: Designed around a children's picture book; useful for relation and sequence exercises, not as an advanced critique authority.

title: Making the Image: Mother and Child
evidence_scope: Official agency article uses a contact sheet and exact final image to show subtle changes of framing, lighting, subject, and selection over a sequence.
limitations: Retrospective account around one celebrated photograph; contact-sheet lessons must be translated into testable selection criteria.

title: Susan Meiselas on Imagination and Photographic Education
evidence_scope: First-party discussion of Meiselas's photographic education books and project prompts spanning gesture, light, portrait disguise, imagined landscape, and collage.
limitations: Projects are prompts for exploration, not evidence that one visual solution is universally superior.

title: The Coast
evidence_scope: First-party discussion of a long-term Indian project and how photographs, moving image, text, and book form create multiple readings.
limitations: Project-specific practice; not a general recipe for sequencing or representing violence.

title: Carolyn Drake Explores Atlanta through the Lens of James Baldwin
author_org: Magnum Photos / Carolyn Drake / High Museum of Art
evidence_scope: First-party work-in-progress interview on researching place and using literature while developing a long-term photo-based project.
limitations: Development process is unfinished and context-specific; literary reference is not a substitute for visible photographic structure.

title: One Influential Image: David Hurn
evidence_scope: First-person account of one influential photograph and its place in a photo essay, useful for separating method influence from surface imitation.
limitations: Autobiographical influence is not an objective quality standard.

title: Dawoud Bey on Photographing People and Communities: Learning Guide
evidence_scope: Official guide page identifies thematic lessons and image-specific questions drawn from Bey's text on photographing people and communities.
limitations: The direct curriculum document timed out during review; verify its full contents before citing a specific exercise or claim.

title: Mary Ellen Mark on the Portrait and the Moment: Learning Guide
evidence_scope: Official guide page confirms a teaching resource focused on portraiture and the moment; Aperture's On Sight curriculum cites its sections on control and forming a relationship.
limitations: Direct guide retrieval timed out during review; verify full guide and exact image references before using it in a pattern.

title: Alex Webb and Rebecca Norris Webb on Street Photography and the Poetic Image: Learning Guide
author_org: Aperture / Alex Webb / Rebecca Norris Webb
evidence_scope: Official page identifies a thematic learning guide on street photography and poetic images.
limitations: Direct page retrieval timed out and the official URL contains a likely slug typo; verify curriculum and exact passages before rule admission.

title: Black Is Beautiful: The Photography of Kwame Brathwaite — Learning Guide
evidence_scope: Official learning-guide page frames a resource for discussing the Black Is Beautiful exhibition and book across ages.
limitations: The page verifies resource scope but not every underlying aesthetic or historical claim; inspect the linked curriculum for specifics.

title: Aperture 240, Native America: Learning Guide
evidence_scope: Official educator resource provides themes, analysis of selected works, and contextual material around Native American photographic representation.
limitations: Issue-specific material; use named contributors and exact works rather than flattening diverse practices into one convention.

title: The True America: Photographs by Ernest Cole — Learning Guide
evidence_scope: Official learning-guide page identifies an educator resource accompanying Ernest Cole's exhibition and book.
limitations: The linked curriculum was not fully inspected; verify exact works, captions, and lesson content before pattern admission.

title: 掌握好光影与色彩就能拍出好看的照片「街头摄影教学」
evidence_scope: Original Chinese-language creator video explicitly focuses on using light, color, and composition in street photography.
limitations: The title promises a broad outcome; inspect the demonstrated frames before converting any slogan into a pattern.

title: 街头不知道拍什么可以参考我的思路和构图
evidence_scope: Original Chinese-language creator lesson framed around field thought process and composition when subject matter is uncertain.
limitations: Self-described experience and follower count are not evidence of teaching effectiveness; extract only demonstrated, testable actions.

title: 自然光人像怎么拍才通透？核心思路在这！
evidence_scope: Original Chinese-language portrait lesson within a larger series covering exposure, light, color, model direction, and story.
limitations: Brand and preset references are present; separate sponsored product framing from visible lighting demonstrations.

title: 第一视角扫街：扫街拍照，这几个构图技巧够用了
evidence_scope: Original first-person Chinese street lesson connects field choices, visual references, personal observation, and intended expression.
limitations: Includes a phone-brand campaign tag; distinguish the creator's process demonstration from product promotion.

title: 旅行摄影的构图技巧：原来这么拍第77集
evidence_scope: Original Chinese travel-photography program episode describes composition as organizing a three-dimensional scene into a two-dimensional frame through focal length, viewpoint, and timing.
limitations: One program episode and one presenter's approach; verify individual demonstrations before generalizing.

title: B站最全面的零基础学摄影教程：人像引导、逆光与构图
evidence_scope: Original Chinese creator series combines camera basics with portrait direction, backlight, composition, and practical demonstrations.
limitations: Promotional claims such as rapid level gains are not evidence; review individual lessons and examples separately.

title: 我是如何进行景深堆栈的
evidence_scope: Official Bilibili-channel lesson demonstrates a specific landscape focus-stacking workflow in Chinese-accessible form.
limitations: Technical workflow solves focus-plane coverage only; it does not establish composition or meaning, and stacked images require disclosure where relevant.

title: Sean Tucker Photography
evidence_scope: Creator's official site defines tutorials as practical craft joined to light, intention, storytelling, and expression, with distinct portrait, street, and rural practices.
limitations: Self-description and portfolio claims are not independent proof; cite a specific tutorial or work for a concrete method.

title: Jamie Windsor Photography and YouTube
evidence_scope: Creator's official biography states that his educational channel combines practical craft with cultural, philosophical, and ethical questions about image making.
limitations: An index and self-description; inspect individual videos and cited works before accepting a critique claim.

title: Wildlife Photography Essentials
evidence_scope: Creator's official course page describes a sixteen-module wildlife curriculum and a separate Lightroom processing course.
limitations: Sales-page scope is verified, not course effectiveness or the accuracy of every lesson.

title: Top Tips to Get into Wildlife Photography
evidence_scope: First-party video gives a bounded introduction to starting wildlife photography from a working nature photographer.
limitations: Use demonstrated field practices only after checking safety and current local wildlife rules.

title: Mark Denney Landscape Photography Education
evidence_scope: Creator's official site offers landscape shooting and editing education, including a before/after account of using existing RAW light for depth, direction, and atmosphere.
limitations: Commercial course and newsletter claims require independent testing; avoid equating dimensional editing with objective quality.

title: Journal of Wildlife Photography Training
evidence_scope: Specialist education platform describes workshop-level articles, courses, critique, fieldcraft, behavior, light, and image-making with named instructors.
limitations: Commercial self-description and membership count do not establish outcomes; validate individual instructors and lessons before rule use.

title: Best of Photojournalism Visual Integrity Guidelines
evidence_scope: Current competition guidance reproduces NPPA ethics and gives concrete capture and post-production restrictions for visual journalism.
limitations: Applies to photojournalism and this competition; disclosed art, commercial, and conceptual practices can follow different rules.

title: PPA Code of Ethics
evidence_scope: Professional association code covers honesty, integrity, client and colleague relationships, and inclusion.
limitations: Broad professional conduct code; it gives little image-specific guidance and should not drive aesthetic critique.

title: Code of Conduct — In the Field
author_org: Nature Photographers Network / Nature Vision Magazine
evidence_scope: Nature-photography community standard prioritizes subject and habitat welfare, access, disclosure, scene integrity, and avoiding baiting or disturbance.
limitations: Community policy rather than law; current local regulations and species-specific guidance still govern field decisions.

title: Guidelines for Digital Manipulation
author_org: Radio Television Digital News Association / NPPA
evidence_scope: Journalism standard states accuracy as the governing principle and rejects alterations that deceive or change editorial content.
limitations: Editorial journalism standard; do not impose it unchanged on disclosed composite, advertising, or conceptual work.

title: Wildlife Photographer of the Year Rules
evidence_scope: Official competition rules define original capture, rights, consent for identifiable people, and submission conditions for wildlife imagery.
limitations: Legally binding contest rules, not a universal aesthetic rubric; check the live edition before advising an entrant.

title: Audubon's Guide to Ethical Bird Photography and Videography
evidence_scope: Detailed field guide covers disturbance, stress signals, distance, nests, baiting, playback, flash, drones, locations, captive subjects, and truthful captioning.
limitations: Bird-specific North American guidance; local law and species expertise may require stricter behavior.

title: Nature First Principles
evidence_scope: Seven-principle framework for responsible, minimal-impact nature photography, including location-sharing consequences.
limitations: Voluntary principles; pair with land-manager rules, permits, and species-specific advice.

title: The Met Open Access API
evidence_scope: Official API documentation for retrieving Met object metadata and identifying records marked public domain and open access.
limitations: Object metadata and rights status support verification; they do not by themselves supply formal interpretation or teaching claims.

title: Fan Ho: On the ‘Decisive Moment’
evidence_scope: Museum-published first-person account of Fan Ho's photographic method during his final visit to Hong Kong.
limitations: One artist's retrospective explanation; test image-specific claims against exact works rather than treating decisive moment as a universal style.

title: Fan Ho — Collection Maker Record
evidence_scope: Official museum index linking twenty-eight collection objects by Fan Ho to exact object records.
limitations: A discovery and verification index; use the individual object page for visual claims.

title: The Goat's Dance: Photographs by Graciela Iturbide
author_org: J. Paul Getty Museum / Graciela Iturbide
evidence_scope: Official exhibition resource combines exact named works, project context, and the photographer's account of collaborative access in Juchitán and ritual work.
limitations: The exhibition selection is not a complete account of Iturbide's practice; graphic ritual content requires context-sensitive teaching.

title: Bill Henson's Untitled
author_org: National Gallery of Victoria / Isobel Crombie
evidence_scope: Senior-curator essay explains Henson's cut-screen process, fragmented space, printing practice, and the exact 1997 work's construction.
limitations: Interpretive museum text about one artist; formal methods do not remove the need to discuss age, nudity, power, and display context.

title: Ideas of Africa: Portraiture and Political Imagination
evidence_scope: Official exhibition resource situates African portrait practices in political imagination and links exact works by represented photographers.
limitations: A thematic curatorial frame, not a universal account of African photography; retain each work's local and client context.

title: Teacher's Guide: Analyzing Photographs & Prints
evidence_scope: Official guide separates observation, reflection, questions, and further investigation and supplies concrete prompts for people, objects, arrangement, setting, purpose, audience, and missing information.
limitations: Designed for primary-source literacy rather than aesthetic scoring; hypotheses still require external verification.

title: Online Courses — Seeing Through Photographs
evidence_scope: Official MoMA course hub documents self-paced photography courses, including Mandarin access and direct artist, curator, and scholar perspectives.
limitations: A course index; cite the relevant unit, work, or interview before deriving a specific rule.

title: Photography
evidence_scope: Official learning page organizes photography through documentary interpretation, posed and unposed images, public image, witness, stories, situations, and the photographic record, with exact collection works.
limitations: A thematic entry point rather than a comprehensive theory or scoring rubric.

title: Capturing Light: The Science of Photography
evidence_scope: Official Getty K–12 art-and-science curriculum connects photographic images to light, sensitized materials, optics, process, observation, and hands-on experiments.
limitations: Technical and educational foundations do not establish universal artistic preferences; adapt age-specific activities for adult deliberate practice.

title: An A to Z of Photographic Processes
evidence_scope: Museum reference describes photographic processes and the material and visual consequences of albumen, calotype, daguerreotype, photogram, and other methods.
limitations: Process identification should remain uncertain when only a compressed reproduction is visible; material history is not an aesthetic score.

title: Linnaeus Tripe: Working Methods
evidence_scope: Museum study connects survey training, viewpoint, informational detail, paper-negative softness, glass-negative sharpness, and historically common hand-retouching of skies.
limitations: Historical commissioned survey practice carries colonial context and cannot be transferred as neutral documentary authority.

title: Julia Margaret Cameron's Working Methods
author_org: Victoria and Albert Museum / Julia Margaret Cameron
evidence_scope: Museum account and artist statements document Cameron's deliberate move toward large close portraits, soft focus, dramatic light, and process marks for emotional effect.
limitations: Intent explains the choice but does not automatically excuse unreadable key regions in another portrait or use case.

title: Garry Fabian Miller: Working Methods
author_org: Victoria and Albert Museum / Garry Fabian Miller
evidence_scope: Artist and museum account details camera-less exposure through colored materials, variation over time, and prolonged assessment of shape, luminosity, density, and presence.
limitations: A specialized darkroom practice; its evaluative vocabulary must be translated carefully for camera-based photographs.

title: Studio, Street and Style: The Photography of James Barnor
evidence_scope: Museum resource connects Barnor's street, studio, fashion, documentary, and color-lab work across Ghana and the United Kingdom, including a calibration image that later became iconic.
limitations: A short overview; use exact works and sitter context before turning historical significance into formal advice.

title: Artist to Artist: Jarod Lew and Reagan Louie in Conversation
evidence_scope: Two photographers discuss form, identity, home, family, community, teaching, and Asian American experience in their practices.
limitations: First-person positions provide context and productive questions, not external validation of every interpretation.

title: New Rules for Storytelling: The Photography of Alejandro Cartagena
evidence_scope: First-person discussion of project photography, family archives, photobooks, collage, collected images, AI, and a deliberate challenge to decisive-moment storytelling.
limitations: The artist's ‘documentary cubist’ method is one position; AI and archival reuse require work-specific disclosure, rights, and provenance review.

title: Kunié Sugiura's Photopainting: One Second with Eternity
evidence_scope: Artist interview covers six decades of combining photography with painting, sculpture, installation, photograms, pinhole methods, and experimental color.
limitations: Medium expansion offers alternatives rather than default fixes for conventional photographs.

title: The Voracious Eye of Wolfgang Tillmans: A Conversation with the Artist
evidence_scope: First-person interview connects everyday subjects, photocopy enlargement, direct photography, abstraction, installation constellations, and questioning how viewers look.
limitations: The artist's broad installation logic cannot be reduced to ‘everything matters’ as an excuse against selection or hierarchy in a single image.

title: Artist Talk: Jeff Wall on Walker Evans
evidence_scope: Photographer and curator discuss photographic finding, vernacular subjects, influence, and the relationship between Wall's practice and Walker Evans.
limitations: An artist-to-artist interpretation; reference exact discussed works before using it to diagnose a user's image.

title: Artist Talk: Wendy Red Star
evidence_scope: Artist talk addresses photography, sculpture, performance, cultural heritage, archival research, and recasting historical narratives from an Apsáalooke perspective.
limitations: Do not generalize one artist's cultural position or treat archival intervention as permission to detach materials from community context.

title: Judging the 2021 World Press Photo Contest: Specialized Juries
evidence_scope: Official interviews document genre-specific jury composition and bounded considerations including narrative arc, connection to subjects, surprise, technicality, and avoidance of subject-only cliché.
limitations: Jury comments describe a competition and a particular year; they are evidence of professional deliberation, not timeless objective weights.

title: 摄影吴师自通 摄影课程
author_org: 摄影吴师自通 / 吴玮
evidence_scope: Twenty-five-part Chinese course index includes the meaning of composition and critique, compositional means and elements, camera maintenance, and multiple product-photography demonstrations.
limitations: The current upload is not clearly the original publication and some material is dated; verify authorship and test individual demonstrations before rule use.

title: 从零学摄影：摄影师必学的透视关系
evidence_scope: Original Chinese-language course episode focuses on perspective as a relation distinct from generic composition and color recipes.
limitations: One short creator lesson; preserve optical accuracy and compare its examples with primary technical references before rule admission.

title: 摄影构图技巧大全：22节课程
evidence_scope: Long-form Chinese course index covers pre-composition thinking, camera position, line and plane, visual force, contrast, layering, repetition, and rhythm.
limitations: Promotional title and unclear institutional provenance lower confidence; use as a discovery map and validate each principle against stronger sources and images.

title: 4种构图，解锁电影级摄影美学
evidence_scope: Creator's original short lesson demonstrates four bounded compositional approaches for prepared portrait scenes and explicitly notes that content and ideas remain more important than technique.
limitations: A concise style-oriented tutorial; do not equate cinematic cues with story or apply its four forms as a checklist.

title: 别再胡乱调色了：后期修图的正确步骤
evidence_scope: Chinese post-processing series index connects tonal categories, histogram reading, color fundamentals, color space, and a proposed editing order.
limitations: Creator identity and every lesson claim are not independently verified; software operations and strong marketing language require comparison with official color and application documentation.

title: 第一视角：武汉旧城街头摄影
evidence_scope: Original first-person street-photography video states a project intent around people continuing daily life amid urban change and preserving dignity rather than rescue spectacle.
limitations: A small contemporary creator's self-description; critique the resulting frames independently and do not treat stated intent as proof of visual success.

title: Composition in Photography: Let's Start Here
author_org: The Art of Photography / Ted Forbes
evidence_scope: Verified creator video presents a specific long-used composition exercise rather than only a list of named templates.
limitations: A creator's exercise is not a universal composition theory; inspect the full demonstration and measure transfer on independent images.

title: Apply Masking for Local Adjustments
evidence_scope: Current official documentation defines local masking tools, add/subtract refinement, feathering, and the tonal and color controls that can be applied selectively.
limitations: Software capability does not justify where or how strongly to edit; automated masks require edge inspection and the latest version may differ.

title: Retouch Photos: Sharpening and Noise Reduction
evidence_scope: Official documentation distinguishes edge-contrast sharpening from luminance and color noise reduction and describes detail-versus-smoothing tradeoffs at 1:1 view.
limitations: Sharpening cannot restore truly missed focus, and noise-reduction settings are image-, output-, and version-dependent.

title: Upright Automatic Perspective Correction in Lightroom Classic
evidence_scope: Official documentation explains level, vertical, full, and auto transformations, recommends lens profiles first, and notes crop reset behavior.
limitations: Converging lines may be intentional; perspective correction changes framing, stretches content, and can force cropping.

title: Adjust Image Tone and Color in Lightroom Classic
evidence_scope: Official documentation describes tonal scale controls, highlight and shadow clipping indicators, color and grayscale adjustments, and histogram feedback.
limitations: Histogram endpoints do not determine expressive correctness; intentional clipping and output conditions require image-specific judgment.

title: EE367 / CS448I: Computational Imaging
evidence_scope: Current university syllabus situates aperture, depth of field, exposure, sensors, noise, HDR, tone mapping, denoising, and deconvolution within a formal computational-imaging curriculum with assignments and evaluation.
limitations: An advanced engineering course, not an aesthetic-critique syllabus; technical correctness cannot by itself establish a photograph's expressive success.

title: Understanding Maximum Aperture
evidence_scope: Official educational article explains the coupled effects of aperture on exposure, shutter-speed options, and depth of field, and recommends test frames rather than a single universal setting.
limitations: Beginner-oriented and brand-published; depth of field also depends on focus distance, focal length, format, viewing conditions, and acceptable sharpness.

title: Understanding Focal Length
evidence_scope: Official educational article defines focal length through angle of view and magnification and compares broad lens-use cases across architecture, landscape, portrait, wildlife, nature, and product photography.
limitations: Perspective relationships are governed primarily by camera position; focal-length categories and subject recommendations are starting points, not aesthetic rules.

title: Bokeh for Beginners
evidence_scope: Official article explicitly connects visible background blur to aperture, focal length, camera-to-subject distance, subject-to-background distance, highlight structure, and diaphragm shape.
limitations: Pleasant blur is not automatically meaningful separation, and the article's preference for smooth bokeh is genre- and intention-dependent.

title: Taking Close-up Photos
evidence_scope: Official guide relates minimum focus distance, reproduction scale, lens choice, aperture, image stabilization, and tripod use to close-up sharpness and framing.
limitations: Camera-specific shortcuts and a single suggested aperture do not replace magnification-dependent depth-of-field tests, wind control, focus stacking, or subject-specific lighting.

title: Photographing Sports Indoors and Out
evidence_scope: Official guide joins position, anticipation, peak action, background control, directional space, autofocus, exposure tradeoffs, equipment details, and post-action emotion in one bounded sports-photography workflow.
limitations: Suggested settings are dated, equipment-specific starting points; access, safety, sport rhythm, desired motion rendering, and venue rules override them.

title: History of the Annual World Press Photo Contest
evidence_scope: The institution's history documents how categories, jury structures, professional contexts, and notions such as an 'artistic' press image changed over decades, cautioning against treating one contest result as timeless consensus.
limitations: An institutional self-history is not an independent audit and does not supply a universal ranking system for personal, commercial, or staged photography.

title: 2025 World Press Photo Contest Winners Jury Report
evidence_scope: A year-specific primary record of how regional and global juries articulated the strengths, context, representation, and ethical stakes of selected contemporary documentary work.
limitations: Contest-specific deliberation from one year; use as evidence of stated professional reasoning, not as proof that the winners exhaust good documentary practice.

title: The Artist Initiative: Stewardship of Color Photography
author_org: San Francisco Museum of Modern Art
evidence_scope: Museum research frames color photographs as material objects whose reprinting, preservation, display, and artist intent can alter how color decisions should be understood beyond a screen preview.
limitations: A conservation initiative does not prescribe color grading for every digital file; production and viewing conditions must remain explicit.

title: Curtis Moffat: Working Methods
evidence_scope: Collection-based account uses portraits, contact sheets, crop markings, snapshots, photograms, and color-process artifacts to show iteration across pose, lighting, angle, cropping, and material technique.
limitations: Historical reconstruction combines surviving artifacts and curatorial interpretation; do not translate studio glamour conventions directly into contemporary documentary critique.

title: 100 Years of Fashion Photography
evidence_scope: Museum survey tracks shifts among controlled studio work, movement-led pictures, photojournalistic spontaneity, naturalism, and editorial subcultures across a century of fashion photography.
limitations: A selective historical survey shaped by collection and exhibition priorities; stylistic sequence is not a ladder of improvement or a universal portrait rubric.

title: Photographing Industry: Maurice Broomfield
evidence_scope: Archive-based essay connects factory knowledge, advance visits, sketches, relationship-building, staged lighting, close human detail, client aims, and later editorial use in Broomfield's industrial photographs.
limitations: Commissioned industrial imagery can aestheticize labor and corporate progress; factual, labor, safety, and power contexts must be assessed alongside visual drama.

title: Soft-Proof Images in Lightroom Classic
evidence_scope: Official documentation explains proof previews, display- and destination-gamut warnings, output profiles, rendering intent, and proof copies for anticipating print-dependent tone and color shifts.
limitations: A soft proof depends on calibrated display, correct profiles, paper and ink simulation, viewing light, and the chosen rendering intent; it does not guarantee a perceptual match.
